vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: social-media-autopilot-api
Version: 1.0.2

The skill bundle is a well-structured, dependency-free CLI client for the SocialEcho API. It uses native Node.js fetch (Node 18+) to interact with documented endpoints (team, account, article, report) and follows security best practices by requiring explicit CLI arguments for API keys rather than attempting to read sensitive environment variables automatically. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection was found across the JavaScript files or the SKILL.md documentation.

llm.summary: The package is a small CLI wrapper that matches its description (calls SocialEcho APIs using an API key); its files and runtime instructions are consistent and proportional to that purpose.

dimensions.detail: The name, SKILL.md, OpenAPI spec and CLI code all align: the scripts perform GET calls to team/account/article/report endpoints and require a Team API key passed at runtime. Minor metadata mismatch: registry owner ID (kn7ax...) differs from _meta.json.ownerId (socialecho-net) and there is no homepage — you may want to verify publisher identity before trusting keys.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent/user to run the provided CLI scripts with explicit --api-key and optional --base-url/--team-id/--lang; the code only reads process.argv and calls the declared API endpoints. There are no instructions to read unrelated files/env vars or to transmit data to unexpected endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec; this is effectively instruction + bundled Node CLI files (no external downloads or npm dependencies). That reduces install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime requires a Team API key (passed via --api-key) which is appropriate for the described API calls. The skill declares no required environment variables — the key is a CLI argument. Consider that whoever/whatever invokes these scripts must supply the API key; ensure your agent or CI won't leak keys to unintended endpoints.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent privileges (always:false). It does not modify system or other-skill configurations and has no install-time hooks that demand elevated access.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears coherent and implements a simple CLI client for SocialEcho's public API. Before installing or using it: 1) Verify the publisher (registry owner ID vs _meta.json differ and there's no homepage) — only provide real team API keys to code from a trusted source. 2) Run the scripts in a controlled/dev environment first (use --base-url api-dev) and test with a limited/dev API key. 3) Be aware you must supply the Team API key to the script at runtime; ensure the agent or automation invoking the CLI won't accidentally forward that key to an attacker-controlled base-url. 4) Review the included client.js yourself — it prints the response body and URL (this can reveal query params or endpoints) so avoid passing sensitive values in ways that could be logged by downstream systems.
